name: Kentucky
note: In Kentucky the funeral director who first takes custody of the body files the death certificate with the Cabinet for Health and Family Services. Filing goes through the Kentucky Electronic Death Registration System. The physician has five working days to certify the cause after the funeral director presents the certificate. A provisional certificate filed with the local registrar must come before any burial, removal or other disposition. Cremation also needs a coroner's permit. The statute is unusually open: the state registrar issues a certified copy to 'any applicant', and an annual list of all deaths is an open record. State law sends deaths onward only to the State Board of Elections, which must purge a voter within five days of notice and receives the lifetime death file every year.

steps.title: Determine death under customary medical standards
steps.who: Whoever determines death under usual and customary medical standards. Brain death needs two licensed physicians.
steps.summary: Kentucky defines death by statute. KRS 213.076(1)(c) also refers to 'the physician pronouncing death' as an alternative certifier.

steps.title: Report coroner's cases to the coroner and police
steps.who: Any person, hospital or institution that finds or has the body. A licensed embalmer, funeral director or ambulance service first at the scene must also notify.
steps.trigger: A death in any of the KRS 72.025 categories: homicide or violence, suicide, drugs, unexplained deaths, deaths in custody, cremation without past medical history, and others.
steps.summary: The body may not be moved until the coroner directs. The coroner must require a post-mortem examination in the listed circumstances.

steps.title: Refer deaths more than 36 hours after last attendance to the coroner
steps.who: The certifier or funeral director handling the certificate.
steps.trigger: Death more than 36 hours after the decedent was last treated by a physician, APRN, PA, dentist or chiropractor.
steps.summary: The coroner investigates and certifies the cause. If no coroner or deputy is available, the county judge/executive appoints someone.

steps.title: Coroner signs the certificate in coroner's cases
steps.who: The county coroner. For a natural death they may authorise the physician or APRN of record to sign.

deadline.text: within five days after receiving results of the inquiry

steps.summary: If a later autopsy changes the findings, the coroner must notify the Vital Statistics Branch.

steps.title: Funeral director takes personal particulars from the informant
steps.who: The person best qualified to give the particulars, over their signature and address. The funeral director must also ask whether the deceased served in the military and give a burial-rights fact sheet.
steps.trigger: The funeral director taking custody of the body.
steps.summary: The funeral director who first takes custody of the body is responsible for the certificate.

steps.title: Present the certificate to the medical certifier
steps.who: The funeral director. The certificate goes to the attending physician, APRN or PA, or the physician who pronounced death, or the health officer or coroner as the state registrar directs.

deadline.text: within five days of the death

steps.summary: The certifier must complete, sign and return the medical part within five working days of presentation.

steps.title: Provisional certificate filed with the local registrar before disposition
steps.who: The funeral director. For a death in an institution, it may be filed with the person in charge of the institution, who must not release the body until it is.
steps.trigger: Before burial, vault, cremation, other disposition, or removal from the registration district.
steps.summary: A signed copy of the provisional certificate authorises possession, transport and (except for cremation) disposition. Sextons may not inter a body without it. The local registrar is an employee of the local health department.

steps.title: Coroner's permit before cremation
steps.who: Anyone who cremates, or transports a body for cremation.
steps.summary: The county coroner issues a permit stating the cause of death. The permit is filed with the local registrar after cremation. Cremating without it is a Class D felony (KRS 213.991(1)).

steps.title: Funeral director files the certificate through KY-EDRS
steps.who: The funeral director or person acting as such.
steps.trigger: Return of the completed medical certification.

deadline.text: prior to final disposition (provisional certificate); no fixed day count for the final certificate

steps.summary: All certificates go to the Cabinet for Health and Family Services (Vital Statistics Branch) through the Kentucky Electronic Death Registration System. Wilful neglect of a chapter 213 duty is a Class B misdemeanor.

steps.title: Certified copies to any applicant
steps.who: The state registrar. Any applicant may get a copy. Copies requested at filing are issued within two working days. The Vital Statistics Branch also gives the funeral director three free verification-of-death statements.

deadline.text: copies requested at filing issued within two working days

steps.summary: The statute puts no eligibility test on certified copies, unlike most states.

steps.title: State registrar sends copies or data to local health departments
steps.who: The state registrar, to each local health department, on an agreed schedule.
steps.latencyNote: "establish a schedule with each local health department" (ky-213-031)
steps.summary: The copies remain the property of the Vital Statistics Branch.

steps.title: Data to the federal vital statistics agency
steps.who: The cabinet, to the federal agency responsible for national vital statistics.
steps.summary: Data are supplied on a cost-sharing basis, for statistical use only.

steps.title: Death notices and the annual lifetime death file to the State Board of Elections
steps.who: The Cabinet for Health and Family Services (or another reliable source), to the State Board of Elections, which then notifies the county clerk.
steps.trigger: Notification of a death. The full lifetime death records are also sent each year by 1 July.

deadline.text: name removed within five days of notification; county clerk updates within ten days

steps.summary: The board purges the voter within five days, except while registration books are closed for an election. The county clerk updates county files within ten days.

steps.title: Copies or data to public agencies on request
steps.who: Federal, state and local agencies asking the cabinet.
steps.summary: Agencies may receive data for statistical or administrative purposes on terms set by regulation. No statutory feed to the Transportation Cabinet (driver licences), Medicaid or the Department of Revenue was found.

steps.title: Private agencies: data on request, but nothing for commercial purposes
steps.summary: Private agencies may receive data for statistical or administrative purposes, but only statistical data for commercial purposes. In practice a private body either buys a certified copy as 'any applicant' or relies on the family.

steps.title: Annual alphabetical list of deaths is an open record
steps.summary: The list gives the name, date and county of death of everyone who died in Kentucky. It is open to public inspection on request.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: No day count. A provisional certificate must be filed before final disposition, and the funeral director must present the certificate to the certifier within 5 days of death. The certifier then has 5 working days.

informantDuty.note: The funeral director who first takes custody of the body files. The informant only supplies particulars.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: Coroners get coroner's cases (KRS 72.025 list, deaths more than 36 hours after last attendance) and every cremation needs a coroner's permit. There is no independent review of all certificates.

electronicRegistration.note: All certificates of death are filed through the Kentucky Electronic Death Registration System. The provisional certificate before disposition is a separate document filed with the local registrar.

centralPopulationRegister.note: No population register. The Vital Statistics Branch keeps an event register and shares copies with local health departments.

governmentPropagation.note: Kentucky statute requires onward notice only to the State Board of Elections. No statutory feed to driver licensing, Medicaid or state tax was found. Federal feeds are in the us-federal layer.

certificateAccess.note: KRS 213.136(1) requires the state registrar to issue certified copies to any applicant. Regulations under KRS 213.131(1) were not checked for added conditions.

privateSectorVerification.note: There is no verification service. Private agencies may receive data for statistical or administrative purposes (no commercial use beyond statistics), anyone may buy a certified copy, and the annual death list is an open record.

gaps: Kentucky administrative regulations (901 KAR chapter 5, vital statistics) were not read. They may add identification or eligibility conditions to KRS 213.136(1)'s 'any applicant' rule, so certificateAccess 'open' rests on the statute alone.

No KRS section was found that requires the Vital Statistics Branch to notify the Transportation Cabinet (driver licences), Medicaid (KRS 205) or the Department of Revenue. Chapter 186 catchlines were scanned for death-related sections.
KRS 116.116 (agreements with federal agencies to identify deceased or non-citizen voters) takes effect on 1 January 2028 and is not reflected as a step.
Who may pronounce death outside a physician (e.g. nurses, coroners) was not traced. KRS 446.400 only sets medical standards and requires two physicians for brain death.
The 'verification-of-death statements' given to funeral directors (KRS 213.076(6)) are not defined in statute, so their use by banks and insurers was not established.
Statute PDFs have stray spaces inside some words. Quotes were chosen from clean spans.
